(2) Include the whole word "harbor" ignoring case. (3) Do not use the whole word "urgent" ignoring case. (4) No digits. (5) Exactly 2 nonempty paragraphs separated by a blank line. (6) Begin exactly "Dear team,". (7) End exactly "Kind regards.".

Dear team, The harbor sample remains on the review table. The re-usable folders belong beside the front-desk register while the meeting room is closed. Each team member can read the plain-language summary before choosing an after-lunch meeting slot. An easy-to-read note can describe the changes without repeating every step in yesterday's message. A well-timed reminder gives everyone a chance to re-read the agreement before the hand-off. We can ask the group's point-person to gather the left-over papers after the final check. A short pause gives the note-taker time to compare the room's layout with the written plan. We shouldn't replace the working copy with a draft whose check-in notes haven't been reviewed. An up-to-date list will help the day-shift staff prepare for the next hand-over meeting. This week's follow-through depends on a clear statement from the review team's co-ordinator. Please keep the meeting's pre-work separate from the notes that still need a second check. The back-up record belongs in the shared folder rather than the personal note-book on the desk.

Kind regards.
